script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A dimly lit room. A large painting of a tree dominates one wall. A middle-aged MAN, JAMES, sits on a leather armchair, brooding. He clutches a small, worn-out notebook in his hands, his gaze lost in its pages.

JAMES
(speaking to himself)
Ten years... I've been here for ten years. And what have I achieved?

His wife, CAROLINE, enters the room. She is a kind, gentle woman, in her late forties, with a warm smile.

CAROLINE
(concerned)
James, you look troubled. What's on your mind?

James stands up, his eyes still fixed on the notebook.

JAMES
I've been working on this novel for ten years, Caroline. And it's still not good enough.

Caroline approaches him, her expression sympathetic.

CAROLINE
You've written a great deal. Perhaps it's time to let go of this one and start another.

James shakes his head, his face contorted with frustration.

JAMES
No, I won't give up. This novel is my legacy, my magnum opus. It has to be perfect.

EXT. PARK - DAY

James walks through the park, deep in thought. He passes by a group of young CHILDREN playing. They laugh and shout, their joyful noise echoing through the park.

James stops at a bench, gazing at the children. He watches as they play, their innocence and happiness a stark contrast to his own turmoil.

INT. JAMES' STUDY - DAY

James sits at his desk, the same worn-out notebook open before him. He stares at the blank pages, his mind racing.

Suddenly, there's a knock at the door. It's VICTOR, a former classmate and long-lost friend. Victor is a successful businessman, confident and charismatic.

VICTOR
(surprised)
James, is that you? It's been ages!

James looks up, his face a mixture of anger and disappointment.

JAMES
Victor. I'd almost forgotten about you.

VICTOR
(amused)
Well, I've certainly not forgotten about you. I heard about your novel. It's quite a legacy you're building there, James.

JAMES
(sarcastically)
Yes, a legacy of failure.

VICTOR
(grinning)
Come now, James. It's not all bad. You've spent ten years perfecting your craft. That's admirable.

James scoffs, his frustration mounting.

JAMES
Perfecting my craft? I've barely scratched the surface.

VICTOR
(leaning forward)
You know what I think? I think you're being too hard on yourself. You've allowed the fear of failure to consume you.

JAMES
(angrily)
Fear of failure? This isn't about fear. It's about ambition. About striving for greatness.

VICTOR
(smiling)
Then perhaps you've been going about it the wrong way. Ambition isn't about perfection. It's about progress. About moving forward, even when it's difficult.

James pauses, considering Victor's words.

JAMES
What would you suggest I do?

VICTOR
(serious)
Finish that novel. Send it out into the world. Even if it's not perfect, even if it's not your magnum opus, it's still a step forward.

James looks at Victor, a glimmer of hope in his eyes.

JAMES
You really think so?

VICTOR
(nods)
Absolutely. But you have to believe it too.

INT. LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Caroline sits on the armchair, her eyes glued to a laptop screen. James enters the room, his face looking less troubled.

JAMES
(proudly)
I've finished it, Caroline. I've finished the novel.

Caroline looks up, her eyes shining with pride.

CAROLINE
(smiling)
I'm so proud of you, James.

JAMES
(determined)
This is just the beginning.

EXT. SUBURBAN STREET - NIGHT

James walks down the quiet suburban street, the glow of the streetlights illuminating the darkened pavement. He feels a sense of calm and contentment.

JAMES
(to himself)
I've done it. I've finished the novel. And it's not the end. It's just the beginning.

FADE OUT.

---

THE END.
